newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UIP reaches deal with EU on pay TV licensing rules.
newsitem.headline: UIP reaches deal with EU on pay TV licensing rules.

text.p: UIP, a joint venture between Hollywood studios Universal, Paramount and MGM, said on Friday it had resolved issues with the European Comission relating to its pay television operations.
The agreement, which affects only the European Union territory, calls for the three studios to "license their pay TV rights in the future without using the facilities of UIP."

"UIP Pay Television is pleased to have reached this resolution with the European Commission. It ends a protracted and complex set of proceedings, is consistent with the studio's business practices, and meets the ongoing objectives of both the studios and EU competition policy," it said in a statement.
UIP said the settlement was separate from the Commission's evaluation of UIP's film distribution rules in Europe which still awaits a final decision.

The distribution arm of the three U.S. cinema studios has long been accused by its European rivals of operating a "block booking" system, forcing cinemas to buy film packages to get Hollywood blockbusters. UIP has denied the accusations.
Last year the Commission raided its premises in London, Paris and Brussels.

UIP has long requested a renewal of a 1988 exemption from EU competition rules which allows it to distribute the films for Paramount, a unit of Viacom, Universal and MGM, in the EU. -- Brussels newrroom 322 2876841
